A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Nova assembly-language-model research by the same authors, despite extensive redesign. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original binary similarity, cross-architecture translation, and source-code recovery experiments, including model-generated examples and appendix embedding comparisons.

after.justification: v3 reports original executable decompilation and binary similarity results, component ablations, and embedding and attention analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v1's StarCoder-based Nova/Nova+ uses language modeling followed by optimization generation and optimization-level prediction. v3 replaces these auxiliary tasks with functionality and optimization contrastive learning, introduces instruction-summary tokens and hierarchical attention, and uses DeepSeek-Coder as its backbone (Sections 2–3). These change the architecture and training procedure substantially.

E1.justification: v3 adds AnghaBench pretraining and evaluates HumanEval-Decompile plus Binutils, Curl, ImageMagick, SQLite, OpenSSL, and Putty. Generated/Codeflaws and BinaryCorp testing disappear; BinaryCorp remains BCSD fine-tuning data. ARM64 coverage and cross-architecture translation are removed. Binary recovery continues as decompilation, so that terminology change does not itself introduce a new task.

E2.justification: For BCSD, v3 retains jTrans and adds evaluated comparisons with DiEmph and CodeArt. For recovery/decompilation, GPT-3.5 remains, GPT-4 and LLM4Decompile are added, and v1's published-score comparisons with Coda and Neutron disappear (v1 Tables 2–7; v3 Tables 2–8).

E3.justification: BCSD changes from twelve optimization directions at pool sizes 32 and 10,000 to O0-to-O3 retrieval at sizes 50, 100, 200, and 500, with Recall@1 replacing MRR-focused reporting. Decompilation uses executable Pass@1/10 evaluation instead of lexical recovery metrics. Model scales, preprocessing, and fine-tuning budgets also change; v3 specifies one fine-tuning epoch rather than v1's two.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's Nova/Nova+ comparisons and illustrative cases, v3 introduces component ablations removing contrastive learning and hierarchical attention on both retained tasks. Section 4.3 and Appendices A.4–A.7 add decompilation cases, PCA/t-SNE visualizations, embedding-distance analyses, and layer/head attention analyses addressing how the proposed components affect representations.

E5.justification: v3 newly presents embedding-distance distributions as boxplots (Figure 13) and specifies 20 sampled decompilations per assembly for Nova and LLM4Decompile (Section 3.2). These add distribution and sampling information, but neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v1's BinaryCorp, Generated, and Codeflaws results are replaced by new benchmark and ablation results. For example, v1 reports Nova+ MRR 0.727 at pool size 10,000, whereas v3 reports Nova-6B average decompilation Pass@1 of 29.42% and average Recall@1 of 0.67 at pool size 500. These are different-condition results, not directly comparable performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2.3 introduces quantified constraints separating same-function and different-function embeddings, an ordering constraint across optimization levels, and corresponding contrastive losses and a combined objective. Its BCSD loss also differs from v1's cosine-similarity softmax formulation. These are substantive mathematical changes, although neither version contains theorem-and-proof developments.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes the first generative binary LLMs, two optimization-related pretraining tasks, and superiority across three downstream tasks. v3 centers its contributions on hierarchical attention, contrastive learning, and representation analyses, with two-task performance claims headlined as improvements up to 146.54% for decompilation and 6.17% for similarity detection.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking functionality clustering, optimization-distance ordering, attention entropy, and instruction-summary attention to its mechanisms. Its limitations emphasize X86-only coverage and untested larger models. v1's explicit inability to capture global dependencies and discussion of restoring normalized addresses and calls are removed, changing the stated applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 Appendices A.1–A.3 document contrastive-data filtering, 1,024/2,048-token limits, loss weighting, revised batch sizes and learning rates, and eight 40GB A100 GPUs. v1 instead specifies its normalization pipeline, cross-compilation environment, and A5000/A10 infrastructure. The new truncation and filtering disclosures provide substantial additional implementation information without establishing that equivalent settings existed in v1.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning around recent assembly models, discussing CodeArt, SLaDe, and LLM4Decompile and adding DeepSeek-Coder, SimCSE, and attention-analysis literature. It replaces v1's broad first-generative-binary-LLM positioning with distinctions concerning architecture and assembly-specific training, and removes the separate disassembler discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and explanatory narrative are extensively rewritten around security applications, low information density, and optimization diversity. Related work moves after the results, training details move into an expanded appendix, and the conclusion/limitations order changes. The appendices are reorganized from task examples into implementation details and analyses.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the motivation and overview figures and introduces attention-mask diagrams, contrastive-learning illustrations, embedding projections, boxplots, and attention heatmaps. Tables are redesigned around decompilation optimization levels, individual BCSD projects, and ablations. These substantially replace v1's three-task schematics, architecture-by-metric tables, and large code-example displays.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation through executable decompilation tests, contemporary baselines, component ablations, and appendix representation analyses. This addresses v1's reliance on similarity metrics that can reward incorrect recovery: Figure 8 gives incorrect code 100% token accuracy. Coverage narrows, and reporting defects weaken exact claims: v3 Table 4 repeats a Pass@10 baseline row under Pass@1, while Table 2's Nova-1B scores average 20.695%, not 22.09%. Despite these defects, the improvement in assessing functional correctness and explaining component effects is substantial.
